decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered the federal funds rate by 75 basis points to a new target range of 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to establish a target range for the federal funds rate of 0 to 1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed lowered rates into a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent, moving away from a single target number.

changes.quote: Since the Committee's last meeting, labor market conditions have deteriorated, and the available data indicate that consumer spending, business investment, and industrial production have declined.
changes.explanation: The Fed highlighted broad economic weakness, noting that jobs, spending, business investment, and production are all falling.

changes.quote: Meanwhile, inflationary pressures have diminished appreciably.
changes.explanation: Falling commodity prices and weak economic activity have significantly reduced inflation pressures.

changes.quote: In particular, the Committee anticipates that weak economic conditions are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for some time.
changes.explanation: The Fed signaled that interest rates will likely stay exceptionally low for a prolonged period to support the economy.

changes.quote: The focus of the Committee's policy going forward will be to support the functioning of financial markets and stimulate the economy through open market operations and other measures that sustain the size of the Federal Reserve's balance sheet at a high level.
changes.explanation: With interest rates near zero, the Fed is shifting its focus to unconventional tools, including massive asset purchases, to support credit and financial markets.

tone_quotes.quote: Since the Committee's last meeting, labor market conditions have deteriorated, and the available data indicate that consumer spending, business investment, and industrial production have declined.
In particular, the Committee anticipates that weak economic conditions are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for some time.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 11.94% APR, a 75 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $3.12.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.37% and moved -16 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.53% would fall by about $30.04 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $45.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 6.8%, and employers added an average of -557k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.1% over the past year (November 2008); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -2.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -10 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.63% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed intends to keep borrowing costs exceptionally low for an extended period while relying on balance sheet expansion to heal credit markets. Educational forecast models suggest the next meeting has a 52% chance of a hold, a 39% chance of a cut, and a 9% chance of a hike.
